name: Slow Cooker Mississippi Pork Bowls
intro_html: Mississippi pork is that tangy, buttery, ranch-and-pepperoncini magic, and it works just as well on pork as it does on the classic pot roast. Piled over potatoes with carrots, each bowl brings {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings out of one pot keeps the whole week covered.
ingredients_display: Au Jus Gravy Mix: 1 (1 oz) packet (65 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Ranch Seasoning Mix, 1 packet: ~$0.67. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 1oz packets.
Au Jus Gravy Mix, 1 (1 oz) packet: ~$2.25. Buy 3 1oz packets: $2.90.

Batch total: about $42.60 across 14 servings, so roughly $3.04 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $47.73 across 14 servings, roughly $3.41 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $3.22 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $50.95. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Potatoes are one of the cheapest bases going. An 8 lb bag runs cheap and doubles as your starch, so skip buying rice for this one.
One packet of ranch seasoning does all the flavor work. No need for a cabinet full of separate spices.
A jar of pepperoncini lasts a long time in the fridge, so the third of a jar you use here costs next to nothing per bowl.
make_it: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker and surround it with the potatoes and shredded carrots.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix and the au jus gravy mix over everything.
Add the pepperoncini along with a splash of their juice, then lay the butter on top.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Shred the pork and stir it through all those buttery, tangy juices.
Whisk the cornstarch with a splash of cold water, stir it into the juices, and let them bubble a minute or two until the sauce thickens.
Divide the pork and potatoes into your containers.
portion_html: Every serving comes in around {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Salt & Lavender, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Tangy, hearty, and dead simple. Set it in the morning and dinner takes care of itself. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
